issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning followed by unreachable break conflates warning semantics with hard error
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a warning class meant for warnings.warn(), but the code raises it as an exception and follows it with a dead `break`. The author hasn't decided whether this is advisory or fatal. Pick one: warn-and-continue via warnings.warn, or raise a real exception like ValueError/ZarrShardMisalignmentError. Remove the unreachable break either way.

issues.description: Unresolved design question shipped as code: warn vs raise vs config-precedence
issues.detail: The PR description itself asks whether shard/config mismatch should raise, warn, or prompt a config change, and the code ships without answering. Decide the precedence rule (shard shape wins for correctness; config is advisory) before merging so the implementation matches the intent.

issues.description: Divisibility check only inspects dw[0] while iterating, assuming uniform chunks across the tuple
issues.detail: auto_chunks/normalize_chunks return per-axis tuples with potentially non-uniform tails. The loop iterates all axes but only reads dw[0], so the stated invariant (every axis chunk divides the shard) is under-checked. Either state and prove dw[0] is representative in a comment, or check all chunks and report the offending axis.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size uses prod over all axes, giving wrong remediation for per-axis misalignment
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` is the total shard byte volume, but the failure is per-axis. Telling a user to set array.chunk-size to the full shard volume overshoots when only one axis is misaligned. Derive the recommendation from the actual alignment requirement, and drop the spurious max(1, itemsize) guard.

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` is a precedence trap; use `% != 0`
issues.detail: Python parses this correctly as `not ((n % zw) == 0)`, but it forces the reader to consult the precedence table. `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` is the literate equivalent and avoids future review confusion.

issues.description: Test weakened — only asserts first-axis divisibility, losing the original two-block coverage
issues.detail: The previous test asserted the exact chunk tuple (block size and block count). The new `all(c % s == 0 for c, s in zip(result.chunksize, zarr_shard_shape))` only checks the nominal first block on each axis, not the remainder block nor the count. Restore the stricter assertion to keep the test honest about what it proves.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The core idea — using shard shape as previous_chunks so auto_chunks lands on shard-aligned multiples — is sound, but the new safety check ships with two glaring defects: a warning class raised as a hard exception, followed by an unreachable `break`. The divisibility check iterates all axes but only reads dw[0], and the suggested remediation uses prod-over-all-axes shard bytes, misleading users when only one axis is misaligned. The PR description's own open question (warn vs raise vs reconfigure) must be resolved before merge, and the regression test should restore the stricter chunk-tuple assertion.
